title: Teacup Chihuahua: Breed Guide Of A Hidden Pet
author: Buzz Tum
contentHtml:
Teacup Chihuahuas are incredibly tiny dogs known for their vibrant personalities. This guide will help you understand everything about these pint-sized pets. You'll learn about the specific traits that define a Teacup Chihuahua, how to properly care for them, and the common health issues they face. Discover the joys and challenges of owning one of these miniature companions and see if a Teacup Chihuahua is the perfect addition to your family.

Have you ever wanted a dog to carry around with you almost anywhere you could go? teacup Chihuahua puppies have exuberant personalities and adorable looks that capture the hearts of all who see them. They love dogs with their owners and always have enough personality to keep you entertained. Families with older children or single families are a perfect fit for this dog and look forward to spending their time with you. Read on to learn all about this mini little dog …

What Is A Teacup Chihuahua? (Overview)

Teacup Chihuahua puppies are proud members of the Toy Breed group according to AKC.

These exuberant pups will let you know what they have in mind. They make a great companion dog for the right owner and because they are so small, they won’t take up much space.

Miniature Chihuahuas can be quite high maintenance with their constant demands and bathroom breaks. They will need exercise just like other dogs but are not suitable for long walks

Since they are so small, they will need access to food all day. Just like with any dog, they will need to be properly socialized and trained by their owners to help them become the best companion possible.

Teacup Chihuahua Breed Guide

  • Overview: Teacup / Toy.
  • Purpose: Comrade.
  • Weight: ~ 5 lbs.
  • Size: ~ 6 inches.
  • Temperament: Loyal, gritty and attentive.

Pros and Cons

Professionals:

  • Suitable for apartment living.
  • Loyal and affectionate to their owners.
  • Highly adaptable to life situations.
  • Excellent travel companion.
  • Lifelong puppy appearance.

Versus:

  • Not suitable for young families.
  • Socialization is extremely important from a young age.
  • He can be aggressive with strangers.
  • Highly dependent on their owners (separation anxiety).

Appearance Of The Teacup Chihuahua

 

Their bodies are compact and muscular with legs shorter than their length. They have fine bones which give them delicate features, with a tail that curls upwards.

Cut it

With the AKC breed standard for a 6-pound Chihuahua, a Teacup Chihuahua is usually under 5 pounds in size.

These dogs will stand around six inches tall.

Coat and Colours

teacup Chihuahua puppies can have a variety of different colours and coat types.

The most common colours include black, blue, chocolate, cream, white and red. Although many Chihuahuas you see can be a mix of these colours such as two-tone or tricolour.

They may also have merle markings with masks of different colours. This leaves for a variety of different colours for your Chihuahua.

These dogs can have a smooth coat (short coat) or a long coat.

A smooth coat will be short, soft and shiny. While long coats will be soft with a straight or slightly wavy texture. It should be a thick coat with feathers on the limbs.

6 Curiosities About Miniature Chihuahuas

  1. There is a specific gene found only in Chihuahuas that can be linked to an ancient breed of dog in pre-Columbia.
  2. Chihuahuas are known to be the smallest dogs in the world.
  3. Due to their small size, they are often born by caesarean section from a veterinarian.
  4. The breed’s name comes from a state in Mexico called Chihuahua.
  5. Some have a molera (soft spot on the head) from the skull bones that don’t fully fuse.
  6. Tea Chihuahuas have been artificially bred by humans to create a better companion.

Teacup Chihuahua Personality And Temperament

 

Chihuahuas are confident, they will surely capture anyone’s heart.

Just like their looks, these dogs too have a puppy-like playfulness for they are always willing to entertain and play with their toys.

Teacup Chihuahuas love to be with their owners and depend on you for your love and attention.

You will notice that they have a lot of energy for short periods, which is great for a quick walk or play. They have been known to wear out playing and running around your house – as they are so small this can usually happen in just one room.

Although Chihuahuas are very affectionate, they can also be very protective of their owners. This means they can be barkers since they want to alert you to whatever is going on.

They also need mental stimulation due to their alert and witty personalities.

They are known for having great personalities. This means these dogs will rule your home if not properly trained.

Even though they are small, these dogs should be trained and socialized just like any other breed. They can be stubborn during their training, but with the right love and diligence, they can become fantastic friends for life.

They are small dogs with a large dog complex and can be snappy when encountering strangers or small children.

This means they need socialization and training from a young age to help them realize that strangers can turn into friends too. Once comfortable, these dogs will continue with their loving and playful disposition.

Caring For A Teacup Chihuahua

 

Mini Chihuahuas can be high-maintenance dogs mainly because of their personality.

They are very needy when it comes to your attention, but as long as they have it and can be with you they will be fine.

This little dog is great for city life as they are small and perfect for an apartment.

They have a low requirement for exercise and food intake due to their size which could also be beneficial for busy people. However, they may need to increase bathroom breaks to ensure there are no accidents around the house due to their small bladder.

Exercise Requirements

They can be quite an energetic breed but due to their size, they tire quickly.

A short walk once or twice a day will be enough to tire them out.

Little Chihuahuas can also play indoors without making too much noise or destruction as they continue to draw out their energy.

A good walking schedule, potty breaks and playtime will ensure that your dog gets the proper exercise and stimulation he needs. Playing some games in your home like hide and seek will also help you. They can get tired with their toys in small spaces, which is great for older people and busy people.

  • Number of walks per day: 1.
  • Total exercise needed per day: 30 minutes.

Grooming And Shedding

Your care commitments will depend on the specific length of their coat.

If they have short hair, they will need to be brushed once a week and will not have to go to a professional groomer. If your Chihuahua has long hair, you will need to brush them several times a week to keep up with their hair loss.

Their hair can also become matted if left fallow for long periods. Long-haired Chihuahuas will benefit most from going to a groomer. Shedding can also be a problem, so be sure to brush them so your home doesn’t get overrun with hair.

 

Nutrition And Diet

These puppies are so small that they don’t eat much.

The correct food and diet are needed during their specific life stages (puppy, adult and senior).

Due to their size, they need to eat frequently to keep their blood sugar high.

Choosing a dog for small dogs can also help ensure a healthy lifestyle as these foods are made specifically for their specific protein, carbohydrate and fat needs.

Some Chihuahuas can become overweight, so it’s important to make sure they have the correct calorie intake.

Treats should be limited to special occasions or training.

Calories per day: Cups of croquettes per day:
250 ~ 0.5

Known Health Problems

There are a few known health problems for Teacup Chihuahuas listed below:

  • Hypoglycemia
  • Heart problems (such as mitral valve disease).
  • Hydrocephalus.
  • Dystocia.

Due to selective breeding with teacups, these health issues listed above can be made worse, so this is something to be aware of when considering this breed (or any other teacup).

How Long Does a Chihuahua Teacup Last?

You can expect them to live around 14-16 years depending on their environment, health, and genetics.

How Much Does a Chihuahua Teacup Cost?

Depending on the breeder, expect to pay between $ 500 and $ 2,000 for a puppy.

How to Train a Teacup Chihuahua

 

When you train your Chihuahua, you need to make sure that he knows that you are the leader of the family.

As these dogs can have dominance issues, training and socialization are key to their education. They will respond better to positive reinforcement and repetition.

Chihuahuas are very good at picking up on human social cues and want to please their owners. This will make it easier to work with them during their training.

Make sure that as a puppy you don’t allow behaviours that you would not want them to do as an adult. These dogs can be stubborn, so a firm but loving training style will be best..

A good game to play would be to grab a dog gift and place it under one of the three mugs. Move the cups and ask your dog to point to the cup with the treat underneath.

Socialization is a must for these dogs. This can be done by introducing your puppy to friends and their dogs. Since they are so small, make sure other large dogs don’t accidentally injure them. To make sure your Teacup Chihuahua has as many friends as possible, start socializing with them from a young age.

Summary

This is an exuberant, loyal, and intelligent dog who is willing to give you everything he has to become your best friend. They will love you to the end!

Teacups Chihuahuas are highly intelligent, so the need for mental stimulation is a must.

FAQs

How big will a teacup Chihuahua get?

Teacup Chihuahuas are very small, usually weighing between 2 to 5 pounds and standing about 6 inches tall at the shoulder when fully grown.

Do teacup Chihuahuas live long?

Teacup Chihuahuas typically have a lifespan of 12 to 15 years. However, their health depends heavily on their breeding, care, and prevention of common health issues.

Do teacup Chihuahuas need to be walked?

Yes, teacup Chihuahuas need regular exercise like all dogs, but due to their small size, their exercise needs are less demanding. Short, gentle walks are sufficient to keep them healthy and happy.

Can a Chihuahua fit in a teacup?

While the term "teacup" suggests they might fit in a teacup, this is a bit misleading. Teacup Chihuahuas are very small, especially as puppies, but they grow to be too large to fit inside an actual teacup.

Where Can I Find A Teacup Chihuahua For Sale?

When looking for a teacup Chihuahua for sale, it's important to find reputable breeders who provide health clearances for their puppies. Consider checking local breed clubs, reputable pet websites, and rescue organizations that specialize in Chihuahuas.
